# Risk Checklist: Notifications and email

**Purpose**: Validate the quality of the requirements governing R11's highest-risk surfaces — the reach-back into five shipped mutators, the three delete cascades, the recipient-set rules, the send-attempt count, the authorization scoping, the sidebar count, and the eight change gates — before implementation begins
**Created**: 2026-09-06
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Reach-Back Into the Five Shipped Mutators

- [ ] CHK001 Are the writes that must produce an `assignment` row named exhaustively, and is each path's no-write condition — assignee unchanged, cleared, self-assigned, lane reorder — stated per path rather than only in aggregate? [Completeness, Spec §FR-050, §FR-051]
- [ ] CHK002 Is "no mutator's result shape changes" stated as a checkable prohibition rather than only as an *Out of Scope* aside? [Measurability, Spec *Out of Scope*, Plan *Complexity Tracking*]
- [ ] CHK003 Is a requirement stated that each of the five mutators' existing validation, authorization, activity write and refusal order is unchanged, in a form a reviewer can check against the diff line by line? [Traceability, Gate 7, Spec *Obligations*]
- [ ] CHK004 Is the scope of `updateComment`'s new transaction bounded — what it must now cover, and what about that mutator it must not change? [Clarity, Spec §FR-057, *Reconciliations*]
- [ ] CHK005 Is the split between what lands inside the causing transaction (the rows) and what happens only after commit (the mail) stated so the ordering is unambiguous at every one of the five call sites? [Clarity, Spec §FR-041, §FR-064]
- [ ] CHK006 Are the board's inline "Add a card" composer and the Create issue page reconciled as one path, so a reader cannot count a fourth assignment path? [Ambiguity, Spec Clarification 4, §FR-050]
- [ ] CHK007 Is the rolled-back case specified as leaving zero rows and sending zero messages, for every one of the five paths rather than for the comment path alone? [Coverage, Spec §FR-041, §SC-010]

## The Three Delete Cascades

- [ ] CHK008 Do FR-058 to FR-061 state the cascade obligation behaviourally, leaving the mechanism open, so they stay verifiable whether or not `deleteProject`, `deleteIssue` and `deleteComment` are edited? [Consistency, Spec §FR-058–§FR-061, Plan Decision 1]
- [ ] CHK009 Are the cascade acceptance criteria observable — no intermediate moment at which a target is gone and a notification pointing at it is not, and a census proving no other project's rows were touched? [Measurability, Spec §FR-061, §SC-015]
- [ ] CHK010 Is the transitive reach of an issue delete and a project delete — through to their comments' notifications — specified explicitly rather than left to be inferred from the row's target columns? [Completeness, Spec §FR-059, §FR-060]
- [ ] CHK011 Is "deactivation is not a delete" stated alongside the cascades, so the two are not conflated by a reader of that section? [Consistency, Spec §FR-062]

## Recipient-Set Rules

- [ ] CHK012 Is the order in which the recipient filters apply — actor removal, deactivated-user removal, mention-over-comment — fixed, and is `CHECK (user_id <> actor_id)` named as a backstop that must never be the mechanism? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-004, §FR-038–§FR-040]
- [ ] CHK013 Is "deactivated" pinned to the moment the recipient set is computed, with the deactivated-after-the-write case ruled on rather than left open? [Clarity, Spec §FR-039, *Assumptions*]
- [ ] CHK014 Is a project comment's recipient set stated as the explicit `project_member` list, with the membership predicate ruled out by name? [Clarity, Spec §FR-048, §SC-007]
- [ ] CHK015 Is "at most one notification per person per comment" required both of the recipient computation and of a database constraint, with the concurrent-edit case named? [Completeness, Spec §FR-006, §SC-006]
- [ ] CHK016 Where a mention set and a comment set both name one person, is the surviving row's *type* fixed rather than only its count? [Clarity, Spec §FR-040]
- [ ] CHK017 Are requirements defined for a mention token naming no existing user, and for a mentioned person who is not a project member? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-044, §FR-045]
- [ ] CHK018 Is the comment-edit diff bounded by separate requirements — newly named users only, no `comment`-type row, nothing withdrawn for a removed mention? [Completeness, Spec §FR-053–§FR-056]
- [ ] CHK019 Are the events that must notify nobody enumerated, so silence is a stated requirement rather than an absence? [Coverage, Spec §FR-042]

## Send-Attempt Count and the Retry Schedule

- [ ] CHK020 Is the count's numbering fully pinned — 0 at insert, 1 once the immediate send returns, stop at 4 — so "three retries" and "four attempts" cannot be read as conflicting? [Clarity, Spec §FR-007, §FR-067]
- [ ] CHK021 Is the increment's timing — after the attempt returns, never before it is made — stated together with its accepted consequence, a possibly duplicated message? [Completeness, Spec §FR-066, *Assumptions*]
- [ ] CHK022 Is retry eligibility expressed as a clock predicate on the row's own age (age > count × 15 minutes) and explicitly independent of how often the sweep runs? [Measurability, Spec §FR-067, §FR-068]
- [ ] CHK023 Are both stop conditions — the count reaching 4, and the age passing one hour from creation — stated with the tie resolved? [Clarity, Spec §FR-067]
- [ ] CHK024 Is "the send-attempt count reaches no DTO and no response" stated as a checkable absence rather than as an intention? [Measurability, Spec §FR-007, §FR-073]
- [ ] CHK025 Are the restart case (the count survives and the row resumes from it) and the dead- or unconfigured-host case (the write still commits, the response is not delayed) each specified with a measurable criterion? [Coverage, Spec §FR-065, §FR-070, §SC-013, §SC-014]

## Authorization and the Read Boundary

- [ ] CHK026 Is `markAllNotificationsRead`'s cleared set required to be derived server-side from the session, with any client-supplied identifier required to change nothing? [Clarity, Spec §FR-029, `OT-AUTHZ-016`]
- [ ] CHK027 Is a notification belonging to somebody else required to be indistinguishable from one that does not exist, rather than refused as forbidden? [Consistency, Spec §FR-026, §SC-002]
- [ ] CHK028 Is the own-`user_id` read rule stated as binding on readers this feature does not own? [Coverage, Spec §FR-024, §FR-073, *Downstream reach-back*]
- [ ] CHK029 Are the server-side obligations stated per new entry point — malformed identifier refused explicitly and never coerced, origin checked, safe result carrying no configuration or database detail? [Completeness, Spec §FR-031, §FR-072, Gate 3]
- [ ] CHK030 Is the unauthenticated case specified for the route and for each mutator separately, distinguishing a redirect from a refusal? [Coverage, Spec §FR-019, User Story 3 scenario 9]

## The Sidebar Count, Revalidation and the Deep Link

- [ ] CHK031 Is the count required to be unbounded by the list's 200-row cap, and is the cap's interaction with the count and with "Mark all read" specified so it reads as a cap and not a page control? [Consistency, Spec §FR-022, §FR-028, §FR-033, §SC-012]
- [ ] CHK032 Is "the count reaches zero in the same interaction" defined observably — no navigation and no reload in between — rather than as a timing intention? [Measurability, Spec §FR-036, §SC-012]
- [ ] CHK033 Is revalidation on mutation fixed as the only permitted refresh mechanism, with polling, sockets and live push prohibited by name? [Clarity, Spec §FR-036]
- [ ] CHK034 Is the single-row case covered as well as "Mark all read", given FR-036 governs *every* write that changes the caller's unread set? [Gap, Spec §FR-036, Plan open question]
- [ ] CHK035 Is the deep link specified as the `#comment-<id>` anchor R7 already emits, with the no-comment target and the deleted-target case both defined? [Clarity, Spec §FR-014, §FR-015, *Edge Cases*]

## Change-Gate Traceability

- [ ] CHK036 Is every pre-existing file this feature edits traced to the requirement that puts it in the diff, so gate 7 is checkable without reading the code? [Traceability, Gate 7, Plan *Project Structure*]
- [ ] CHK037 Are the Red steps most easily faked named with what each must assert — 0-then-1 for the attempt count, the row's *type* for mention-wins, a full census for every "no row is written"? [Measurability, Gate 1, Plan Principle VII row]
- [ ] CHK038 Is "no dependency is installed" stated with the refused categories named, and is the inherited `clsx` discrepancy recorded as outside this feature so a gate 4 review does not attribute it here? [Clarity, Gate 4, Spec §FR-075, Plan *Complexity Tracking*]
- [ ] CHK039 Is the decision that the three delete mutators gain no statement recorded at requirement level, so its absence from the diff reads as intent rather than as an omission under gate 6? [Gap, Gate 6, Plan Decision 1]

## Assumptions and Open Questions

- [ ] CHK040 Is the inverted layering — the auth sweep importing the notifications feature — recorded with its rejected alternative, so a reviewer meets it as a decision rather than a discovery? [Assumption, Plan *Complexity Tracking*]
- [ ] CHK041 Is the open question about whether one `refresh()` re-renders the shared `(app)` layout carried with a named test and a named fallback rather than left unresolved? [Ambiguity, Plan *Complexity Tracking*, Spec §FR-036, §SC-012]
- [ ] CHK042 Is the prohibition on version bumps, status-log rows and history entries stated where a reviewer of this diff will see it? [Consistency, Plan *Explicitly out of scope*]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
